title: Cyrano de Bergerac
byline: José Ferrer won the Best Actor Oscar for Stanley Kramer's 1950 film of Rostand's play.

evidence.note: Partial check only. I tried to read the full text of the Catalog of Copyright Entries volume for January-June 1977 Motion Pictures (archive.org identifier 1977motionpictur3311213libr). It has a Renewal Registrations section. My fetch tool returned only the first part of the text, which ended in the index at 'Benson', before any 'C' or 'K' entries. The tool's own summary of the rest reported no 'Cyrano', but I cannot treat that as a real negative result. The July-December 1977 volume and the 1978 renewal volumes were not read. The volume at archive.org/details/catalogofcopyrig14libr is Fourth Series Part 4 (Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, January-June 1978, current registrations). Its preface says renewals are not in that part, so it would not show a renewal either way. I could not search the Copyright Office public records, because the site is a JavaScript app that returned no records to my fetch.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Jan-Jun 1977 Motion Pictures, archive.org

evidence.note: The Internet Archive item description reads 'PD due to lack of copyright renewal.' That is the uploader's claim, not a primary record. The file name suggests the upload is a Blu-ray rip. Do not rely on the claim until the renewal volumes and the Copyright Office records have been searched.

Dimitri Tiomkin composed the score. It is a sound film, so the recorded track would normally share the film's own copyright status. Separate publishing rights in the underlying music were not checked.

Based on Edmond Rostand's 1897 French play. The screenplay uses Brian Hooker's 1923 English blank-verse translation, with Carl Foreman credited on the screenplay. I did not fetch a term record for the play or the translation.

editorial:
Cyrano de Bergerac (1950) was produced by Stanley Kramer Productions and released by United Artists. Michael Gordon directed, Carl Foreman wrote the screenplay from Brian Hooker's 1923 English translation of Rostand's play, and Dimitri Tiomkin wrote the score. José Ferrer won the Academy Award for Best Actor for the title role.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not proven. For a film published in 1950, the renewal window ran 1977 to 1978. I could read only the opening part of the January-June 1977 renewal catalog, and it did not reach the 'C' entries. I did not search the rest of 1977 or the 1978 renewals, and I could not search the Copyright Office records. The 'PD due to lack of renewal' label on one Internet Archive upload is an uploader's claim, not a record. Tiomkin's score, the Hooker translation and the Rostand play each raise a separate copyright question that this dossier did not resolve.
faq: Was the 1950 Cyrano de Bergerac renewed?

Not confirmed either way. I could read only the first part of the January-June 1977 renewal catalog and did not reach the 'C' entries. The rest of 1977, the 1978 renewals and the Copyright Office records are unchecked. Run those searches before relying on the print.
Does the score or the source play have its own rights?

Possibly. Dimitri Tiomkin's score and Brian Hooker's 1923 translation, which the screenplay uses, were not cleared in this research. A sound film's track normally shares the film's status, but check the music and the translation separately.
